How to Find My Court Date Online

When Is My Court Date?

Knowing when your court date is scheduled is extremely important if you have been charged with a crime or involved in a civil lawsuit. Your court date is the day you are required to appear before a judge in court. Missing your scheduled court date can result in serious consequences, so it's vital that you know the exact date and time. Here's what you need to know about finding your court date and why it matters.

The legal system can be confusing, and navigating it can be challenging. One of the essential things you need to do when dealing with a court case is to find out your court date. Fortunately, most courts now offer the convenience of accessing your court date online. In this article, we will guide you on how to find your court date online and what to do if you cannot find it.

What is a Court Date?

A court date, also known as a hearing date or trial date, is the specific day and time that you must appear in court before a judge. The court date is scheduled on the court calendar by the court clerk's office. All parties involved in the legal case are required to show up at the courthouse on the designated date.

For criminal cases, the court date is the day you will appear before the judge and potentially enter a plea, face trial, or be sentenced. For civil cases, the court date is when the trial will occur and both parties present their evidence and arguments.

Why is it Important to Know Your Court Date?

There are several critical reasons why you need to know your exact court date and time and make sure to show up:

  • Avoid a bench warrant – If you fail to appear for your scheduled court date, the judge can issue a bench warrant for your arrest. This allows the police to apprehend and detain you until your court hearing.
  • Prevent additional charges – Missing your court date could result in additional criminal charges being filed against you, such as contempt of court.
  • Fight your case – Your court hearing is your opportunity to argue your case before the judge. Missing it could negatively impact your case and lead to unfavorable outcomes.
  • Avoid fines or jail time – For minor offenses, not showing up on your court date could immediately result in fines or jail time. For serious charges, it eliminates your chance to defend yourself.

how to check court date

Ways to Find Your Court Date

There are several ways to locate the date and time of your scheduled court hearing or trial. Here are some steps to find your court date information:

Check Court Paperwork

When you were charged, arrested, or served notice of a lawsuit, you likely received paperwork with details about your court date. The documents may include:

  • Summons – Official notice to appear in court on a certain date.
  • Subpoena – Legal document ordering you to appear in court.
  • Citation – Ticket issued during an arrest with date to appear before a judge.
  • Release documents – Paperwork issued when released from jail may include court date.

Carefully review all paperwork you received to locate the exact date, time, courtroom number, judge name, and courthouse address for your court hearing. Make sure to keep these documents in a safe place for reference.

Call the Court Clerk

If you cannot find written notice with your court date or if you lost your paperwork, call the court clerk's office. The court clerk maintains the judge's calendar and courtroom schedule. Provide them your name, case number, or ticket number and request the scheduled court date.

Write down the date and time they provide you and clarify any questions. Court staff are usually helpful in providing court date information over the phone.

Look Up Court Calendar Online

Many court systems now post public court calendars on their official websites. Search for the court's website where your hearing is scheduled, and look for an online court calendar. Filter by date range and case type or name to hopefully find your court date.

Some online calendars allow you to subscribe and receive email or text alerts about your upcoming court date. Use this tool to confirm the date if available.

Contact Your Attorney

If you have a lawyer representing you for the criminal charges or civil lawsuit, reach out to their office to get your court date. Attorneys track important court dates on behalf of their clients.

Provide them your full name and case information, so they can look up the exact date and time in their records. This ensures you get the correct court date.

Why Finding Your Court Date Online is Important

Knowing your court date in advance allows you to prepare accordingly. It gives you enough time to get your documents in order, gather witnesses if necessary, and make arrangements to be present in court. Missing your court date can result in dire consequences, such as being held in contempt of court or losing your case by default.

How to Find Your Court Date Online

There are two primary ways to find your court date online:

Option 1: Use the Court Website

Most court websites have an online search tool that you can use to find your court date. Here are the steps to follow:

  1. Go to the court website. The website's URL will typically be listed on any legal documents you received.
  2. Look for a link to the court calendar or search tool. This link may be listed under the "Court Records" or "Online Services" section of the website.
  3. Enter your case number, name, or other relevant information as requested by the search tool.
  4. Review the results to find your court date.

Option 2: Use a Third-Party Website

Several third-party websites offer court date search tools that can help you find your court date. However, you need to be careful when using these sites, as some may charge a fee or provide inaccurate information. Here are the steps to follow:

  1. Search for "court date search" or "find my court date" on your preferred search engine.
  2. Look for a reputable third-party website that offers a free court date search tool.
  3. Enter your case number, name, or other relevant information as requested by the search tool.
  4. Review the results to find your court date.

Tips for Finding Your Court Date Online

Here are some tips to help you find your court date online quickly and easily:

  • Use the correct court website. Make sure you are using the website for the court where your case is being heard.
  • Have your case number or citation number ready. This information is usually listed on any legal documents you received.
  • Double-check the date and time. Court dates and times can change, so make sure you verify the information a few days before your scheduled appearance.
  • Contact the court directly. If you are unable to find your court date online, contact the court clerk's office for assistance.

What to Do if You Cannot Find Your Court Date Online

If you cannot find your court date online, don't panic

. There are still several things you can do to find out your court date:

  • Call the court clerk's office. The court clerk can provide you with the date and time of your scheduled appearance over the phone.
  • Check your mail. Sometimes, the court sends a notice with your court date through the mail. Look for any letters or legal documents related to your case.
  • Hire an attorney. If you have hired an attorney, they should have the court date information and can inform you of it.

Things to Know About Your Court Date

Once you determine the date of your hearing or trial, make sure you understand the logistics to arrive on time and prepared:

Arrive Early

It's always recommended to arrive at the courthouse at least 30 minutes early before your scheduled court time. You'll need time to pass through security, find parking, and locate the correct courtroom. This prevents you from being late for your court date.

Dress Appropriately

Make sure to dress respectfully as you would for a job interview. Avoid clothing with words, logos, ripped jeans, shorts, tank tops, or flip flops. Judges take offense to inappropriate attire in their courtroom.

Be Prepared

Bring all evidence, documents, photos, or anything you plan to present in your case. Contact witnesses ahead of time and confirm their testimony. Being organized shows the judge you're taking it seriously.

Notify Job/Family

Inform your workplace and family you'll be occupied on your court date, so they know where you are and adjustments can be made to your schedule. Line up childcare if needed.

Respect Courtroom Rules

Once in the courtroom, avoid talking, chewing gum, using your phone, or disruptive behavior. Be polite and address the judge as "your honor." Follow all instructions from court staff.

What Happens if You Miss Your Court Date?

While it can be tempting to skip out on your court date, the consequences make it an unwise choice:

Bench Warrant

If you fail to appear at your scheduled court hearing, the judge may immediately issue a bench warrant for your arrest. This allows law enforcement to detain you and bring you in for the next available court date.

Additional Charges

Missing court can result in the prosecutor filing new criminal charges against you, such as contempt of court, failure to appear, or obstruction. This adds to your legal troubles.

Harm Your Case

For civil cases, not showing up to court may lead the judge to rule against you by default and award the other party damages. For criminal cases, it hurts your credibility with the judge.

Given the risks, it's critical to know your court date and make arrangements to appear on time. Communicate with your attorney if you foresee any issue making it to your scheduled hearing. Otherwise, an arrest warrant, fines, and serious counts could be added!

Conclusion

Finding your court date online can save you time and effort, and it's essential to prepare for your court appearance adequately. By following the steps outlined in this article, you can easily find your court date online and avoid the consequences of missing it.

FAQs

  1. Do all courts offer online court date searches?
  • No, not all courts offer online court date searches. However, many courts now provide this service for the convenience of the public.
  1. Can I trust third-party websites that offer court date searches?
  • You need to be careful when using third-party websites that offer court date searches. Make sure to use reputable sites and verify any information you receive before relying on it.
  1. What should I do if I miss my court date?
  • If you miss your court date, you can face serious consequences, including being held in contempt of court or losing your case by default. Contact the court clerk's office immediately to explain your situation and request a new court date.
  1. Can my court date change?
  • Yes, court dates can change due to various reasons, such as scheduling conflicts or emergencies. Make sure to double-check the date and time of your scheduled appearance a few days before.
  1. What if I cannot find my case number?
  • If you cannot find your case number, contact the court clerk's office for assistance. You may need to provide personal information, such as your name and date of birth, to verify your identity.
  • What if I lost my paperwork with my court date?
  • Contact the court clerk's office to inquire about your scheduled court date. Provide them your name, case number, ticket number or any other identifying details so they can look up the date in their system.
  • Can I reschedule my court date?
  • You must file a written request with the court to ask for a new court date. There has to be a compelling reason, so talk to your attorney. The judge then decides whether to grant a new date. Don't assume your date is moved.
  • What if I'm sick on my court date?
  • You or your lawyer must immediately notify the court if you are ill on the scheduled date. Be prepared to provide a doctor's note validating your excuse. The judge will determine if you are excused or face a bench warrant.
  • What time should I arrive for my court date?
  • Arrive at the courthouse at least 30 minutes before your scheduled court time. This gives you plenty of cushion to get through security, find parking, and locate the right courtroom. Tardiness is unacceptable.
  • What should I bring to court?
  • Bring any evidence, documents, photos, or items you plan to use in your case. Also bring ID, the court paperwork with your case details, and anything else your attorney recommended. The more prepared, the better.
